constraints.text: Readability is judged by content shape with no length floor on its own; placeholder text is defined once in readability.py and imported by the writer.

Since the 2026-10-04 deploy: 7 items `model:not_substantive`, of which the Nobel physics announcement, llm-mistral 0.16 and datasette-atom 0.11a0 are real content; 50 Reddit link posts, 8 without an article (4 HTTP 403, 4 reddit-internal or galleries, one of them a relative crosspost url that raised ValueError).

Probe 2026-10-06 over 108 labeled cerebro items. A presence wording ('whether the text contains the piece itself ... the article, post, announcement or release note the title refers to') called all 48 real items substantive, 3 of 9 code-passing junk not substantive. A length-avoiding wording called all 48 real items substantive but 0 of those 9 junk items not substantive. The deployed wording caught 9 of 9 and misfired 3 times live.

Replaying the two candidate rules over 45 days of currently-readable Reddit items: `link_without_article` matches 243 (most from before Reddit link posts got article fetching on 2026-09-30) and every sample is a link line followed only by comments; the markdown-link rule matches 3 (a removed-post notice, a markdown-link-only self-post, a link post whose body is one markdown link).
